  "text": "At the hardware store, Martin set a small brass hinge on the counter.

“Anything like this?”

The clerk picked it up and worked it with his thumb.

“Cabinet?”

“Kitchen cupboard.”

“We sell them in pairs.”

“I only need one.”

The clerk went down an aisle. Martin stayed beside a display of seed packets, most of them flowers. Someone had put the peas in with the sweet peas.

The clerk returned with a plastic bag.

“Same size. Holes might be different.”

Martin held the old hinge against the new one.

“They are.”

“You can fill the old holes. Matchsticks and wood glue.”

“I've got toothpicks.”

“They'll do.”

Martin put the bag on the counter.

“Door come right off?”

“Nearly. My daughter caught it.”

“Lucky.”

“She says I should get the kitchen redone.”

The clerk glanced at the hinge again.

“Nothing wrong with brass.”

“That's what I said.”

He hadn't said that. He had stood holding the cupboard door while his daughter cleared the mugs onto the table.

“Need screws?”

“Are they not included?”

“Little ones. I'll give you something longer.”

The clerk counted four screws into a paper envelope and folded it shut.

At home, Martin laid everything beside the sink. His daughter had left the mugs arranged by size, the chipped ones at the back.

He opened the cupboard below and found the wood glue behind a bottle of silver polish. The nozzle was blocked. He fetched a pin, sat down at the table, and began to clear it."
